newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Biota signs new research deal.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Biota signs new research deal.

text.p: Australian biomedical group Biota Holdings Ltd on Tuesday announced it had teamed with a leading research group to jointly develop new anti-viral drugs.
Biota said it had formed a major alliance with the Melbourne-based Biomolecular Research Institute, which Biota called a world-leader in molecular-level drug research.
Biota and the privately run institute will start work initially on a drug to fight respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) which causes a serious flu-like illness, the company said.
Nearly all children will have had at least one RSV infection by the age of two years, it said.
RSV could also seriously affect the elderly and lead to pneumonia, asthma-like symptoms and even death.
Biota, in partnership with pharmaceutical group Glaxo Wellcome Plc, is already pioneering a drug to immobolise the influenza virus once a person has been infected.
The RSV drug would work in a similar way, Biota said.
Under the alliance, Biota will pay the institute a fee for access to its technology as well as royalties on a project-by-project basis.
The institute boasts state-of-the art technology such as x-ray crystallography, computer-aided drug design, nuclear magnetic resonance and electron microscopy, Biota said.
